findings.title: CSV export fails with a 500 error
findings.evidence: 14 users hit a 500 on Export CSV; several escalated to support.

findings.title: Onboarding blocked by phone validation error
findings.evidence: 7 trial users abandoned onboarding at the phone step.

findings.title: No Slack integration available
findings.evidence: 4 users searched for Slack and requested it.

ranked.reason: Severity 5 and the highest frequency (14 users), breaking a core export flow for paying accounts. Fix first.
Severity 4 blocking activation for 7 trial users; directly costs conversions, so it ranks above the lower-severity gap.
A severity-3 feature gap with 4 requests; real demand but not blocking existing users, so it trails the two bugs.

findings.title: Dashboard widgets fail to load
findings.evidence: 9 users refreshed repeatedly with blank widgets.

findings.title: Notification settings fail to save
findings.evidence: 5 users saw 'Could not save settings'.

findings.title: Help center search returns no results
findings.evidence: 3 users got no results for common queries.

ranked.reason: Severity 4 and 9 occurrences on the primary landing surface; a broken dashboard undermines daily use. Highest impact here.
Severity 3 affecting 5 users; a real save failure but scoped to one settings page, so below the dashboard bug.
Severity 2 with 3 occurrences; a discoverability gap that is annoying but non-blocking, so it ranks last.

findings.title: Generate API key button is unresponsive
findings.evidence: 22 developers clicked Generate with no key produced.

findings.title: Upgrade payment fails with a card verification error
findings.evidence: 2 users could not complete a paid upgrade.

ranked.reason: Severity 5 and it blocks revenue directly; even at only 2 occurrences a broken checkout outranks a mid-severity bug because each miss is a lost paying customer.
Severity 3 but very high frequency (22 developers); important and worth batching next, yet not revenue-blocking like the payment failure.

findings.title: No upgrade path shown when the seat limit is reached
findings.evidence: 6 admins hit the seat limit with no way to add seats.

findings.title: Account deletion control is hard to find
findings.evidence: 5 users searched settings for a delete option.

findings.title: Filter selection resets on page refresh
findings.evidence: 8 users lost their filters after a refresh.

ranked.reason: Severity-3 gap that blocks expansion revenue: 6 admins wanted more seats and had no path to buy them. Highest business upside.
Only severity 2 but the highest frequency (8 users) and a cheap bug fix; good effort-to-impact ratio, so it edges out the deletion gap.
Severity 3 with 5 occurrences; a compliance-adjacent gap worth fixing but neither revenue-blocking nor high-frequency, so it ranks last.

findings.title: Data export produces corrupted CSV for large reports
findings.evidence: 3 users reported unreadable files over 50k rows.

findings.title: Report date filter ignores the selected timezone
findings.evidence: 11 users saw off-by-hours totals.

findings.title: No way to schedule recurring reports
findings.evidence: 9 users asked for scheduled exports.

ranked.reason: Severity 4 and 11 occurrences, silently corrupting numbers users trust; wrong data at scale is the biggest risk here.
Severity 5 but rare (3 users, large reports only); serious yet narrow, so it sits just under the widespread timezone bug.
Severity 2 feature gap with steady demand (9 requests); valuable roadmap item but not a correctness or availability issue.

findings.title: Login redirects to a blank page on Safari
findings.evidence: 4 Safari users could not reach the app after login.

findings.title: No bulk-delete action for records
findings.evidence: 7 users searched for bulk delete.

ranked.reason: Severity 4 and it blocks access entirely for affected Safari users; an availability bug outranks a feature gap even at lower frequency.
Severity 3 with 7 requests; strong demand for bulk delete but users can still work around it, so it ranks below the login blocker.

findings.title: Session tokens are not invalidated on logout
findings.evidence: 6 users stayed logged in on shared devices after logging out.

findings.title: Search is slow (>5s) on large workspaces
findings.evidence: 15 users on big workspaces waited over five seconds per search.

findings.title: No dark mode
findings.evidence: 4 users asked for a dark theme.

ranked.reason: Severity 5 security defect: tokens surviving logout is an account-takeover risk on shared devices. Security bugs lead regardless of frequency.
Severity 3 but very high frequency (15 users) and it degrades daily use; strong effort-to-impact case, so second.
Severity 2 cosmetic preference with 4 requests; nice-to-have that ranks last against a security bug and a performance issue.

findings.title: No SSO / SAML login for enterprise
findings.evidence: 10 enterprise evaluators required SSO before rollout.

findings.title: Invite emails land in spam
findings.evidence: 5 admins reported teammates never received invites.

ranked.reason: Severity-4 gap that gates enterprise deals: 10 evaluators named SSO a blocker, so the revenue upside outweighs the mid-severity delivery bug.
Severity 3 affecting 5 admins; a real onboarding friction with an easy workaround (resend), so it trails the enterprise blocker.

findings.title: Webhook deliveries are silently dropped
findings.evidence: 8 integrations missed events with no error surfaced.

findings.title: Timezone is wrong in email digests
findings.evidence: 3 users saw digests stamped in the wrong timezone.

findings.title: Tooltip text overflows on mobile
findings.evidence: 20 mobile users saw clipped tooltip text.

ranked.reason: Severity 4 and 8 occurrences with silent data loss; undetected dropped webhooks erode trust in every downstream integration. Highest impact.
Also severity 4 but only 3 occurrences and cosmetic-adjacent (wrong label, not lost data), so it sits below the webhook data loss.
Highest frequency (20) but only severity 2 and purely visual; a cheap polish item that does not block anything, so it ranks last.

findings.title: No CSV import for bulk record creation
findings.evidence: 12 users wanted to import records instead of adding them one by one.

findings.title: No keyboard shortcuts
findings.evidence: 6 power users asked for shortcuts.

ranked.reason: Severity 3 with the higher demand (12 users) and it removes a painful manual workflow; clear activation and retention value.
Severity 2 with 6 requests; a productivity nicety for power users that ranks below the broader import gap.

findings.title: A customer was double-charged at renewal
findings.evidence: 1 customer was billed twice and requested a refund.

findings.title: Avatar upload fails for PNGs over 2MB
findings.evidence: 9 users could not upload larger profile images.

ranked.reason: Severity 5 billing defect: even a single double-charge is a trust and compliance issue that demands an immediate fix and refund. Frequency is irrelevant here.
Severity 3 affecting 9 users but with an obvious workaround (smaller image); worth fixing soon, yet far below a billing error.

findings.title: Two-factor codes are rejected intermittently
findings.evidence: 7 users were locked out despite correct 2FA codes.

findings.title: No audit log export
findings.evidence: 5 enterprise admins needed audit logs for compliance.

findings.title: Table columns are not resizable
findings.evidence: 11 users wanted to resize columns in the data grid.

ranked.reason: Severity 4 and it intermittently blocks login for 7 users; an auth lockout is an availability and security issue, so it leads.
Severity-3 compliance gap for 5 enterprise admins; unblocks deals and audits, ranking above the cosmetic grid bug.
Highest frequency (11) but only severity 2 and purely ergonomic; a low-effort polish item that ranks last against auth and compliance.
